articles.title: A Practical Guide to Swift Structured Concurrency
articles.summary: Sample summary: an overview of a Practical Guide to Swift Structured Concurrency. This item is demo content, not a real article.
articles.excerpt: Sample excerpt for “A Practical Guide to Swift Structured Concurrency”. Read the original at the publisher for the full piece.
articles.content: This is sample tutorial text written for the TechPulse AI demo. Structured concurrency ties the lifetime of child tasks to a parent scope. Use async let for a fixed number of concurrent operations and task groups for a dynamic number. Cancellation propagates from parent to children automatically, so long-running work should check Task.isCancelled or call Task.checkCancellation at sensible points. Actors protect shared mutable state, and @MainActor keeps UI-facing state on the main thread.

articles.summary: Sample summary: an overview of swiftData Migrations from Day One. This item is demo content, not a real article.
articles.excerpt: Sample excerpt for “SwiftData Migrations from Day One”. Read the original at the publisher for the full piece.
articles.content: This is sample tutorial text written for the TechPulse AI demo. Define a VersionedSchema for your first SwiftData model version even before you need a migration. When the schema changes, add a new version and a SchemaMigrationPlan with lightweight or custom stages. Test migrations by creating a store with the old schema, inserting records, and reopening it with the new plan.
